Indicator 7 tracks the rate of [[koloskopi]] performed on patients with [[psc|Primær skleroserende kolangitis (PSC)]] within the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]]. The indicator measures the proportion of adult PSC patients who receive a colonoscopy within 18 months, a critical screening for colorectal cancer risk. 

In 2023, the national colonoscopy rate was 85%, successfully meeting the stated 85% target [^src1]. Regionally, Midtjylland led with 89%, while Hovedstaden and Syddanmark both achieved 86% [^src1]. Sjælland trailed significantly at 70%, missing the national standard [^src1]. At the departmental level, several pediatric and smaller units fell well below the target; notably, Rigshospitalet Pædiatrisk Klinik reported 50%, and both OUH Svendborg and Aarhus Børn og Unge recorded 0% [^src1]. Conversely, small departments such as Bornholm Medicinsk afdeling and Bispebjerg Abdominalcenter K achieved 100%, though their low patient volumes resulted in extremely wide confidence intervals [^src1].

By 2024, the national rate declined to 81% [^src2]. Despite this drop, the 2024 report outlines a development goal of ≥80%, which all five regions successfully met [^src2]. Syddanmark led the regions at 85%, while Hovedstaden fell to 79% [^src2]. Sjælland demonstrated the most significant improvement, rising from 70% in 2023 to 84% in 2024, effectively resolving its previous shortfall [^src1][^src2]. Nordjylland also improved slightly to 82% [^src1][^src2]. 

Departmental outliers and challenges persisted in 2024. OUH Svendborg improved from 0% to 33%, yet remained far below the target, while Gødstrup Medicinsk Afdeling reported a 0% rate [^src2]. Large university hospitals, including Rigshospitalet (77%) and Herlev (76%), also fell short of the 80% development goal [^src2]. Meanwhile, smaller units like Bispebjerg Abdominalcenter K, Nordsjælland Kirurgisk Afdeling, and SHS Aabenraa maintained 100% compliance, continuing the pattern of small denominators yielding wide confidence intervals [^src2].
